# glisten · v9.0.1

Source: https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/

# glisten

A Gleam TCP server library.  Built on top of `gleam_otp`, it provides a
supervisor over a pool of socket acceptors.  Each acceptor will block on `accept`
until a connection is opened.  The acceptor will then spawn a handler process
and then block again on `accept`.

Below is a simple example that will echo received messages. You can get this up and running with the following:

```
$ gleam new <your_project>
$ cd <your_project>
$ gleam add glisten gleam_erlang gleam_otp
```
Then place this code in `src/<your_project>.gleam`:

```
import gleam/bytes_tree
import gleam/erlang/process
import gleam/option.{None}
import glisten.{Packet}
pub fn main() {
  let assert Ok(_) =
    glisten.new(fn(_conn) { #(Nil, None) }, fn(state, msg, conn) {
      let assert Packet(msg) = msg
      let assert Ok(_) = glisten.send(conn, bytes_tree.from_bit_array(msg))
      glisten.continue(state)
    })
    // NOTE:  By default, `glisten` will listen on the loopback interface.  If
    // you want to listen on all interfaces, pass the following.  You can also
    // specify other interface values, including IPv6 addresses.
    // |> glisten.bind("0.0.0.0")
    |> glisten.start(3000)
  process.sleep_forever()
}
```
TLS is also handled using the `glisten.with_tls` method.  This requires a
certificate and key file path.  The rest of the handler flow remains unchanged.

`glisten` doesn’t provide a public API for connected clients.  In order to hook
into the socket lifecycle, you can establish some functions which are called
for the opening and closing of the socket.  An example is provided below.

To serve over TLS:

```
// ...
pub fn main() {
  let assert Ok(_) =
    glisten.new(
      // omitted
    )
    |> glisten.with_tls(
      certfile: "/path/to/server.crt",
      keyfile: "/path/to/server.key",
    )
    |> glisten.start(port: 8080)
  process.sleep_forever()
}
```
But you can also drop down to the lower level listen/accept flow if you’d prefer to manage connections yourself, or only handle a small number at a time.

```
import gleam/result
import glisten/socket/options.{ActiveMode, Passive}
import glisten/tcp
pub fn main() {
  use listener <- result.try(tcp.listen(8000, [ActiveMode(Passive)]))
  use socket <- result.try(tcp.accept(listener))
  use msg <- result.try(tcp.receive(socket, 0))
  echo #("got a msg", msg)
  Ok(Nil)
}
```
See [mist](https://github.com/rawhat/mist) for HTTP support built on top of this library.

---

# glisten · v9.0.1

Source: https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/index.html

# glisten · glisten · v9.0.1

Source: https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/glisten.html

This type holds useful bits of data for the active connection.

```
pub type Connection(user_message) {
  Connection(
    socket:
```
[socket.Socket](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/glisten/socket.html#Socket),
    transport: [transport.Transport](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/glisten/transport.html#Transport),
    subject: [process.Subject](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_erlang/1.3.0/gleam/erlang/process.html#Subject)(@internal Message(user_message)),
  )
}### Constructors

-
          `Connection( socket:`[socket.Socket](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/glisten/socket.html#Socket), transport:[transport.Transport](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/glisten/transport.html#Transport), subject:[process.Subject](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_erlang/1.3.0/gleam/erlang/process.html#Subject)(@internal Message(user_message)), )#### Arguments- transport
-
                This provides a uniform interface for both TCP and TLS methods.

This is used to describe the connecting client’s IP address.

```
pub type IpAddress {
  IpV4(Int, Int, Int, Int)
  IpV6(Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int)
}
```
### Constructors

-
          `IpV4(Int, Int, Int, Int)`
-
          `IpV6(Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int)`

This is the shape of the function you need to provide for the `handler`
argument to `start`.

```
pub type Loop(state, user_message) =
  fn(state,
```
[Message](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Message)(user_message), [Connection](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Connection)(user_message)) -> [Next](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Next)(
    state,
    [Message](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Message)(user_message),
  )Your provided loop function will receive these message types as the second argument.

```
pub type Message(user_message) {
  Packet(BitArray)
  User(user_message)
}
```
### Constructors

-
          `Packet(BitArray)`These are messages received from the socket
-
          `User(user_message)`These are any messages received from the selector returned from `on_init`

```
pub fn bind(
  builder:
```
[Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message),
  interface: String,
) -> [Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message)This sets the interface for `glisten` to listen on. It accepts the following
strings:  “localhost”, valid IPv4 addresses (i.e. “127.0.0.1”), and valid
IPv6 addresses (i.e. “::1”). If an invalid value is provided, this will
panic.

```
pub fn get_connection_info(
  conn:
```
[Connection](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Connection)(user_message),
) -> Result([ConnectionInfo](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#ConnectionInfo), Nil)Tries to read the IP address and port of a connected client. It will return valid IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, attempting to return the most relevant one for the client.

```
pub fn get_server_info(
  listener:
```
[process.Name](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_erlang/1.3.0/gleam/erlang/process.html#Name)(@internal Message),
) -> [ConnectionInfo](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#ConnectionInfo)Returns the user-provided port or the OS-assigned value if 0 was provided.

`pub fn ip_address_to_string(address: `[IpAddress](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#IpAddress)) -> StringConvenience function for convert an `IpAddress` type into a string. It will
convert IPv6 addresses to the canonical short-hand (ie. loopback is ::1).

```
pub fn new(
  on_init: fn(
```
[Connection](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Connection)(user_message)) -> #(
    state,
    [option.Option](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_stdlib/1.0.0/gleam/option.html#Option)([process.Selector](https://hexdocs.pm/gleam_erlang/1.3.0/gleam/erlang/process.html#Selector)(user_message)),
  ),
  loop: fn(state, [Message](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Message)(user_message), [Connection](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Connection)(user_message)) -> [Next](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Next)(
    state,
    [Message](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Message)(user_message),
  ),
) -> [Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message)Create a new handler for each connection.  The required arguments mirror the
`actor.start` API from `gleam_otp`.  The default pool is 10 accceptor
processes.

```
pub fn with_active_state(
  builder:
```
[Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message),
  active_state: [options.ActiveState](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/glisten/socket/options.html#ActiveState),
) -> [Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message)Set the server’s `ActiveState` for flow control of received packets.
Default is `Once`. Allowed are `Once`, `Active` and `Count(n)` where n > 1.

```
pub fn with_close(
  builder:
```
[Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message),
  on_close: fn(state) -> Nil,
) -> [Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message)Adds a function to the handler to be called when the connection is closed.

```
pub fn with_ipv6(
  builder:
```
[Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message),
) -> [Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message)By default, `glisten` listens on `localhost` only over IPv4.  With an IPv4
address, you can call this builder method to also serve over IPv6 on that
interface.  If it is not supported, your application will crash.  If you
call this with an IPv6 interface specified, it will have no effect.

```
pub fn with_pool_size(
  builder:
```
[Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message),
  size: Int,
) -> [Builder](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Builder)(state, user_message)Modify the size of the acceptor pool

# glisten/socket/options · glisten · v9.0.1

Source: https://glisten.hexdocs.pm/glisten/socket/options.html

Mapping to the `{active, _}` option

```
pub type ActiveState {
  Once
  Passive
  Count(Int)
  Active
}
```
### Constructors

-
          `Once`The server acknowledges every package.
-
          `Passive`Not used by server - for use with low level `tcp.receive`.
-
          `Count(Int)`The server will receive `n`packages before activating again.
-
          `Active`Connection is always active, no flow control.

```
pub type IpAddress {
  IpV4(Int, Int, Int, Int)
  IpV6(Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int)
}
```
### Constructors

-
          `IpV4(Int, Int, Int, Int)`
-
          `IpV6(Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int, Int)`

Mode for the socket.  Currently `list` is not supported

```
pub type SocketMode {
  Binary
}
```
### Constructors

-
          `Binary`

Options for the TCP socket

```
pub type TcpOption {
  Backlog(Int)
  Nodelay(Bool)
  Linger(#(Bool, Int))
  SendTimeout(Int)
  SendTimeoutClose(Bool)
  Reuseaddr(Bool)
  ActiveMode(
```
[ActiveState](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#ActiveState))
  Mode([SocketMode](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#SocketMode))
  CertKeyConfig([TlsCerts](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#TlsCerts))
  AlpnPreferredProtocols(List(String))
  Ipv6
  Buffer(Int)
  Ip([Interface](https://glisten.hexdocs.pm#Interface))
}### Constructors

-
          `Backlog(Int)`Default 1024
-
          `Nodelay(Bool)`Default True
-
          `Linger(#(Bool, Int))`
-
          `SendTimeout(Int)`Default 30_000
-
          `SendTimeoutClose(Bool)`Default True
-
          `Reuseaddr(Bool)`Default True
-

          Default Passive for low level and Once for server.
-

          Default Binary
-

-
          `AlpnPreferredProtocols(List(String))`
-
          `Ipv6`
-
          `Buffer(Int)`
-
